text: Agent Workspace is ServiceNow's own out-of-box workspace, built on UI Builder, aimed squarely at service desk agents and ITSM fulfillers who work a queue of assigned incidents and requests all day long. It isn't a general admin tool, and it isn't meant to replace the Application Navigator for configuration work.

In UI16, an agent opens the Incident list, clicks into a record, works it, then navigates back to the list to pick the next one. Agent Workspace keeps the assignment list and the open record in adjacent panes, both visible on screen at once — selecting a different incident from the list swaps what's shown in the record pane, with no full page reload and no trip back through the Application Navigator at all.

Layered around the open record are contextual panels — collapsible side panels surfacing information related to the record without ever leaving the screen. Typical contextual panels show similar incidents, useful for spotting a recurring issue; knowledge articles that might resolve the exact problem reported; and other related records tied to the same configuration item or the same caller.

The practical effect is that an agent spends far less time navigating and far more time reading and acting. Checking whether a similar incident was already resolved, or whether a knowledge article covers the exact error message, happens in a panel right beside the record instead of a separate search-then-switch-tabs detour — and that saved time compounds across dozens of records every single day.

Agent Workspace also isn't one identical screen handed to every agent. It's configured per role and per implementation using UI Builder — which tables feed the assignment list, which contextual panels appear, which actions show up on a record — so a service desk agent's workspace can look and behave differently from a field-service dispatcher's. Next up: system settings versus personal preferences.
